findings.claim: The selection fallback appends its textarea to document.body, outside an open Modal or Offcanvas. The component's own Trap pulls focus back into the panel, so execCommand('copy') runs with nothing selected, returns true, and the copier reports success while the clipboard is unchanged.
findings.scenario: Take a page on http (insecure context, so navigator.clipboard is undefined) or one where writeText rejects. Open a Bootstrap modal with the default focus: true (Modal.ts:211 calls this.#trap.activate()). Inside the modal, put <pre id=HOST_ID> and <button commandfor=HOST_ID command=--copy>. Clicking Copy follows this sequence: the absent API throws at :60, activation is active at :64, and #copySelection appends the textarea to body at :102. textarea.select() at :103 focuses it. That focusin target is outside the trap element, so Trap.#focus (Trap.ts:75-85) focuses the modal's first focusable. Chromium clears a text-control selection when focus leaves the control, so document.execCommand('copy') at :104 runs over an empty selection and still returns true. Copier.ts:66-68 then emits result.vn.copier with { text } and no error. The paste is the old clipboard content. Offcanvas.ts:173 activates the same trap.
findings.evidence: Copier.ts:102 `document.body.append(textarea)`, :103 `textarea.select()`, :104 `return document.execCommand('copy')`, :66 `if (copied.success && copied.value)` with success emitted at :67. Trap.ts:50 adds a document focusin listener, and Trap.ts:77-85 refocuses inside the container for any target outside it. Modal.ts:211 and Offcanvas.ts:173 activate the trap. No Copier proof runs the fallback with an active trap: all 3 fallback cases use a bare frame.

findings.claim: A true return from execCommand('copy') is treated as proof that the host text was copied. A native `copy` event listener on the page can cancel the event or replace its data, and execCommand still returns true, so result.vn.copier reports { text } for a clipboard that holds something else.
findings.scenario: The page has `document.addEventListener('copy', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); e.clipboardData.setData('text/plain', 'Copied from Example') })` or a copy-protection listener that only calls preventDefault. The clipboard API is absent or writeText rejects, and the user clicks Copy. The fallback's execCommand dispatches the native copy event from the textarea, which bubbles to document. The listener cancels it and the browser writes the listener's DataTransfer (or nothing), yet execCommand returns true. Copier.ts:66-67 emits success with the host text the clipboard doesn't hold.
findings.evidence: Copier.ts:104 returns execCommand's boolean, and :66 `copied.success && copied.value` is the only success test. The textarea's copy event is neither observed nor checked, and its clipboardData isn't compared with `text`. The guide's Copy button section reports the result as the settled write of `text`.

findings.claim: Per-host containment does not cover a plugin's boot selector. If querySelectorAll or matches throws, the throw escapes #initialize and #boot reports it, but the boot of every later plugin is skipped. The scope stays live and routing, so it is left half-initialized with one reportError. Routes, by contrast, isolate selector failures per route.
findings.scenario: Call createVeneer(document, { plugins: [customPlugin, ...createBootstrapPlugins()] }), where customPlugin.boot.selector is '[' or any selector the engine refuses. At :228, `this.#root.querySelectorAll(boot.selector)` throws SyntaxError. #boot (:219-220) reports it and returns, and the for-loop over plugins never reaches the carousel, scrollspy, offcanvas, and tab boot entries. data-bs-ride carousels never cycle and .offcanvas.show panels never initialize, while clicks still route. Before M1 the same throw destroyed the scope and rethrew from the constructor, so the failure was visible. The guide (veneer.md:727) states that selector matching runs inside each route's failure boundary and that initialization continues with the remaining hosts and plugins, but boot selectors get no such boundary.
findings.evidence: Veneer.ts:228 `Array.from(this.#root.querySelectorAll(boot.selector))` and :229 `this.#root.matches(boot.selector)` sit outside the per-host attempt at :234-241. Their only boundary is #boot's single attempt around the whole #initialize (:219). Compare #route :193-203, where `target.closest(route.selector)` runs inside each route's attempt. That isolation is pinned by `isolates selector failures from later routes: %s`, and no boot counterpart exists.

findings.claim: The activation-expiry proofs don't pin the activation gate at Copier.ts:64. Their textarea assertion is vacuous because #copySelection's finally removes the textarea, and nothing checks that focus or selection went untouched. With the gate deleted, the tests' verdict rests only on execCommand returning false without activation.
findings.scenario: Delete the `if (realm.navigator.userActivation.isActive)` gate at Copier.ts:64 so #copySelection always runs. In 'reports the original write rejection after transient activation expires', the fallback appends, selects, and removes the textarea, and its finally (Copier.ts:106) removes it, so `expect(root.querySelector('textarea')).toBeNull()` at :126 still passes. Chromium's execCommand('copy') returns false once transient activation has expired, so the original rejection is still reported and the error assertions at :124-125 still pass. The second half of 'copies without the clipboard API on a real click and reports refusal after activation expires' (:186-193) has the same shape. The gate's purpose, not touching focus and selection without activation, is never observed.
findings.evidence: Copier.test.ts:126 `expect(root.querySelector('textarea')).toBeNull()`. Copier.ts:105-106 `finally { textarea.remove()`. Neither test sets a selection or a focused element before the expired-activation copy, and neither asserts on them afterward.

findings.claim: The result.vn.copier row says a failure carries the platform's DOMException. When the clipboard API is absent, the copier builds its own NotAllowedError, so the row is contradicted by the code.
findings.scenario: On an insecure origin, after activation expires (or when the fallback fails), the result detail.error is the DOMException that Copier.ts:60 constructs, with the message 'The clipboard needs a secure context'. No platform API produced it, but the table row says the platform's DOMException.
findings.evidence: guides/veneer.md:1483 `A failure carries the platform's \`DOMException\``. Copier.ts:59-60 `throw new realm.DOMException('The clipboard needs a secure context', 'NotAllowedError')`. The row also omits the case where Copier.ts:77 wraps a non-DOMException in an 'UnknownError'.

findings.scenario: Copier.test.ts:116 and :182 both read `// Chromium's activation window lasts five seconds; the budget also permits scheduling delay.`

findings.claim: `#owner()` and `#target` accept a touch or pen session's item as the source of any native drag. While a pointer session holds an item, an unrelated native drag over that host or a host in its group, such as an external file or a mouse drag from another host, is accepted with dropEffect `move`. Its drop moves the touch-held item.
findings.scenario: On a touchscreen laptop, a finger holds item X's grip in host A past the slop, so A's `#item` is X and X carries `data-vn-dragging`. With the mouse, the user drags a file from the desktop, or an item from host B, onto host A or onto a group host C. In C, `#target` calls `#owner()`. In A, `this.#item?.parentElement === this.#element` is true at line 135. In C, the `[data-vn-dragging]` scan returns A. Then dragover calls preventDefault, sets dropEffect `move`, and draws the indicator for X. The drop calls `#relocate(X, slot, 'pointer', A)`, which moves X under the finger. `owner.#finish(true)` then ends A's touch session while the finger is still down. The file, or B's item, never moves.
findings.evidence: Lines 135 and 139-148 identify the source only by `owner.#item` and `data-vn-dragging`. A touch session sets `#item` in `#begin` at line 272, and nothing marks that item as a pointer-path item. `#target` at lines 364-366 does not check whether the owner's session is native. The guide at line 1638 says the pointer path 'refuses external text and files', and at lines 1675-1676 it says the pointer path moves an item only within its own host.

findings.claim: `#scroll` sends both axes' steps to the single nearest ancestor that overflows on either axis, and it passes that container's full client box rather than the part on screen. A container partly outside the viewport, or one that scrolls on only the other axis, takes the step and the page is never scrolled. This contradicts `DragScrollInput.box`, which is documented as 'the container's visible rectangle'.
findings.scenario: (a) A 390 px phone shows a list inside `<div style="overflow-x:auto">` whose content is wider than the wrapper, on a page taller than the viewport. During a touch drag the finger rests at the viewport's bottom edge. The loop stops at the wrapper because of the overflowX test at lines 305-306. If the wrapper's bottom lies below the viewport, y is 0. Otherwise, the y step goes to `wrapper.scrollBy`, which cannot scroll vertically. Either way the page never scrolls. (b) A card with `max-height:80vh; overflow-y:auto` has its bottom 100 px below the viewport because the page is scrolled. Its bottom edge zone is off screen, so a finger at the viewport bottom is more than 48 px from `box.top + box.height`. computeScroll returns y = 0 and neither the card nor the page scrolls. `touch-action: none` on the grip blocks panning, so items beyond that edge can't be reached during the drag.
findings.evidence: Lines 299-311 choose one container on overflow in either axis. Lines 313-320 build the box from `getBoundingClientRect()` plus `clientWidth` and `clientHeight` and never intersect it with the viewport. No step falls through to the viewport. The `box` TSDoc in types.ts at line 30 reads 'Supplies the container's visible rectangle in viewport coordinates.'

findings.claim: The container walk stops at `document.body` and treats body as the viewport, so a body that is its own scroll container never auto-scrolls. The guide says 'the host's nearest scrollable ancestor' takes the step.
findings.scenario: An app shell sets `html{overflow:hidden;height:100%} body{overflow:auto;height:100%}`. Because html is not `overflow: visible`, body's overflow does not propagate to the viewport, and body is the real scroller. A touch drag toward the bottom edge reaches body in the loop and stops. The guard at line 311 then sets the target to `document.scrollingElement` (html). html does not overflow, so `scrollBy` does nothing and the list never auto-scrolls.
findings.evidence: Line 300 reads `while (container && container !== root && container !== document.body)`, and line 311 reads `const target = container && container !== document.body ? container : root`. The guide at lines 1679-1680 reads 'While the pointer sits in an edge zone of the host's nearest scrollable ancestor, or of the viewport when no ancestor scrolls'.

findings.claim: No proof pins that a touch or pen session removes its four document listeners. If `touch?.session.abort()` were deleted, every case would stay green, even though the guide claims the listeners are removed and that an idle controller holds none.
findings.scenario: Delete line 586. `#finish` still clears `#touch`, so a leaked listener's `#track` returns at line 224 and nothing visible changes. Every session would leave a `pointermove` listener, plus `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, and `lostpointercapture` listeners, on the document until the page unloads. The touch cases in Drag.test.ts and the listener-count case in plugins.test.ts (`command and drag listeners require composition and are released on destroy`) still pass, because that case counts only `click` and `dragstart` listeners.
findings.evidence: plugins.test.ts lines 365-391 call `countCDPListeners` for 'dragstart' and 'click' only. A grep of tests/src/browser/drags for `'pointermove'` finds one hover recorder at Drag.test.ts line 1109 and no listener count. The guide at lines 1703-1707 reads 'An idle controller holds no listeners ... A touch or pen session listens on the document for `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, and `lostpointercapture` events ... and removes those listeners when the session ends.'

findings.claim: `#arm` refuses a non-primary pointer and any pointer whose `button` value isn't 0, but the guide says a touch or pen press arms a session on any handle that a `dragstart` event would admit, 'with the same refusals'. A press that starts after another finger is already down never starts a drag. Because the grip sets `touch-action: none`, that press doesn't pan the page either.
findings.scenario: On a tablet, a thumb rests on the screen outside the list, then the index finger presses a grip and moves 40 px. That `pointerdown` has `isPrimary: false`, so `#arm` returns at line 205. No session starts, and `touch-action: none` on the grip stops the pan, so the gesture does nothing. A pen eraser press (`button` 5) is refused the same way. The guide's list of refusals names neither case.
findings.evidence: Lines 203-208 refuse on `this.#touch || this.#item || !event.isPrimary || event.button !== 0 || !this.#admits(...)`. The guide at lines 1656-1657 reads 'A `pointerdown` event whose `pointerType` value is `touch` or `pen` arms a session on a handle that a `dragstart` event would admit, with the same refusals, `aria-disabled` included.'

findings.claim: No proof covers the guide's claim that the viewport auto-scrolls when no ancestor scrolls. The only auto-scroll case uses a scrollable host and asserts that the page stays at `scrollY === 0`. If the `viewport` branch broke, for example a wrong box or a `scrollBy` on the wrong element, every case would stay green.
findings.scenario: Replace `root` with `document.body` at line 311, or zero out the viewport box at line 313. The case `scrolls a scrollable host on each touch move in its edge zone and holds still while the touch rests` drives only a host with `height:150px;overflow-y:auto`. The `reads the page scroll during a vertical touch drag from $name` cases move 80 px up from y ≈ 284, which never enters the viewport's 48 px zone, and the `touch-action:none` row asserts `scrolled: false`. All of these cases still pass.
findings.evidence: Drag.test.ts lines 1052-1096 assert `expect(scrollY).toBe(0)` with a scrollable host. In the DRAG_TOUCH_ACTIONS cases at lines 1007-1050, the moves at steps 10, 20, 40, and 80 never reach the viewport edge zone. The guide at lines 1679-1680 claims '...or of the viewport when no ancestor scrolls', and at lines 1808-1809 it cites only the scrollable-host case.

findings.claim: `#group()` collects every same-valued host in the document, including one nested inside the item being moved. A crossing key, a `--forward` command, or a native drop then targets a host inside the moved item. The target emits an unprevented `move`, then `moveBefore` and the `insertBefore` fallback both throw HierarchyRequestError. The item stays in place, `end` reports `moved: false`, and the error reaches `reportError`.
findings.scenario:
1. Author host A (`data-vn-drag="g"`) whose item X contains a nested host B (`data-vn-drag="g"`), followed by host C (`data-vn-drag="g"`).
2. Focus X's grip and press Alt+ArrowRight, or click X's `--forward` button.
3. `#group()` returns [A, B, C] in document order, so `#cross` picks B, a descendant of X.
4. `B.#relocate` emits `move.vn.drag` on B with no prevention, then calls `B.moveBefore(X, ...)`. The DOM refuses to insert a node into its own descendant and throws a DOMException (HierarchyRequestError).
5. The fallback `#insert` calls `insertBefore`, which throws the same error, and nothing catches it (lines 546-553).
6. `#finish(false)` emits `end` with `moved: false`, and the router reports the error.
Result: a data-owning listener that applied the unprevented `move` to its model is now out of sync with the DOM. A native drag of X onto B's area takes the same path: `#owner()` admits X, so dragover is accepted and the drop throws.
findings.evidence: Line 123: `for (const host of this.#element.ownerDocument.querySelectorAll('[data-vn-drag]'))`. Nothing excludes a host that the moved item contains. `#owner()` (lines 139-148) has the same gap. `#relocate` emits `move` at line 532 before the DOM move at lines 546-553, and that move has no containment check. The guide says only that "The group order is the hosts' document order" and says nothing about nested hosts.

findings.claim: `#group()` lists only hosts that already have a live registered controller (`this.#context.component(host)` looks up and never creates). Crossing keys and the `--backward`/`--forward` commands therefore skip a group host inserted after boot, or one whose controller was destroyed, until that host receives input of its own. A native drag reaches the same host because the route creates its controller on dragenter. This contradicts the guide's statement that the pair moves the item to the previous or next host in document order.
findings.scenario:
1. After `createVeneer` boots, the app inserts a third empty column `<ul data-vn-drag="parcels" aria-label="Shipped">` after Loading dock. This is a plausible step when a board grows.
2. Focus a Loading dock grip and press Alt+ArrowRight, or click its `--forward` button. Because Shipped has no controller, `#group()` returns [Packing queue, Loading dock], and nothing happens.
3. Insert the new host between the two existing hosts instead. Alt+ArrowRight from Packing queue then skips it and lands in Loading dock.
4. Dragging the same item onto Shipped with the mouse works, because the dragenter route creates the controller.
The guide states that boot has no mutation observer and that "the drag plugin discovers later hosts through input events". For keyboard and command crossing, the target host receives no input, so it is never discovered.
findings.evidence: Lines 124-128: `const controller = host instanceof realm.HTMLElement && host.getAttribute('data-vn-drag') === group ? this.#context.component(host) : undefined; if (controller) controllers.push(controller)`. `Registry.context().component` is lookup-only (src/browser/Registry.ts:56), while the route path in `buildPlugin` (src/browser/helpers.ts) calls `plugin.create` when no component exists. Guide: "moves the focused item to the previous or next host in document order".

findings.claim: No proof checks the group boundary of the crossing keys or the transfer commands. Only native drag is tested between hosts of different or empty groups. Removing the value comparison or the empty-value guard in `#group()` would leave every test green. The guide still lists "refusals between hosts outside one group" among the routing proofs, and claims that "A host outside every group leaves the crossing pair alone".
findings.scenario:
1. Change `#group()` so it compares no group values, or drop its `if (!group) return controllers` guard.
2. With hosts 'parcels' and 'returns', Alt+ArrowRight or `--forward` now moves an item into the other group. An ungrouped host now calls preventDefault on Alt+ArrowLeft and Alt+ArrowRight.
3. Every existing case still passes:
- `DRAG_GROUP_REFUSALS` drives only a native drag, which goes through `#owner()`.
- `DRAG_TRANSFER_AXES` and the `--forward`/`--backward` case use two 'parcels' hosts.
- The ungrouped row-axis case has no neighbor host and never checks `defaultPrevented`.
findings.evidence: `it.each(DRAG_GROUP_REFUSALS)('refuses a native drag between hosts with $name', ...)` is the only use of the refusal fixture. `renderDragGroup(['parcels', 'parcels'], style)` (line 601) and `renderDragGroup()` (line 660) are the only keyboard and command crossing fixtures. Guide lines 1821-1822: "group transfers by native drag, crossing keys, and transfer commands, refusals between hosts outside one group".

findings.claim: The comment added by commit 45f60fa narrates the approach that was tried and replaced (the grip's lower quarter). `.claude/rules/writing.md` § Code comments forbids this: "Do not narrate history, alternatives tried, or a probe's result".
findings.scenario: A reader of the journey finds a comment about a target (the grip's lower quarter) that the code no longer uses. That history belongs in the commit message, which already records it.
findings.evidence: `// The board items wrap at 390 px, so a point in the grip's lower quarter sits above the / item's midpoint; the item's own height places the drop past it at every journey width.` The commit message for 45f60fa reads: "The case targeted the lower quarter of the Garden hose grip ... The drop now targets the list item".

findings.claim: The `#press` method writes `aria-pressed` onto every `button[commandfor]` whose `commandForElement` is the host, whatever its `command` value. The plugin's clear projection at src/browser/wakes/plugins.ts:44-46 does the same. Buttons that invoke a different command on the same host become pressed toggles. The route selector at plugins.ts:24 and the guide ("A different command creates no wake controller", guides/veneer.md:1150) both limit the family to `command="--wake"`.
findings.scenario: A `<dialog id="recipe">` is the wake host and has three buttons pointing at it: `<button commandfor="recipe" command="show-modal">Open recipe</button>`, `<button commandfor="recipe" command="close">Close</button>`, and `<button commandfor="recipe" command="--wake">Keep screen on</button>`. Clicking Keep screen on runs `#press(true)`, which stamps `aria-pressed="true"` on Open recipe and Close as well. Assistive technology then announces them as pressed toggle buttons, and a later release flips them to `"false"`. A section that is both a fullscreen host and a wake host has the same problem in both directions: wake intent is written onto the `--fullscreen` button, and fullscreen state is written onto the `--wake` button.
findings.evidence: Wake.ts:155-157: `for (const button of this.#element.ownerDocument.querySelectorAll('button[commandfor]')) { if (button instanceof realm.HTMLButtonElement && button.commandForElement === this.#element) button.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(pressed)) }`. plugins.ts:44 uses the same `'button[commandfor]'` query. The route selector is `'button[command="--wake"][commandfor]'`. guides/veneer.md:1164 reads "Every bound button reflects intent through `aria-pressed`".

findings.claim: The routing proof says it updates every bound button at change time, but nothing in it depends on the plugin's clear projection (plugins.ts:36-49). Wake.#press writes `aria-pressed` synchronously, before every change or error event this test produces. The only case where the projection does unique work is an external sentinel release, which emits a change without `#press`, onto a button inserted after acquisition. No case with a composed scope drives that.
findings.scenario: Delete the whole `clear` block from createWakePlugin. Every assertion in the test still passes. After the first click, `#press(true)` has already written `'true'` to both buttons before the change event fires. The inserted button `added = button.cloneNode(true)` is a clone that already carries `aria-pressed="true"`. The release click runs `#press(false)` on all three buttons before the sentinel's change event. The guide's claim that "The plugin finds buttons in the host document after a change, including buttons inserted after acquisition" (guides/veneer.md:1164-1165) therefore has no failing case.
findings.evidence: plugins.test.ts:71-80: `const added = button.cloneNode(true); root.append(added); await userEvent.click(button) ... toEqual(['false', 'false', 'false'])`. Wake.ts:122 calls `#press(false)` in release() before the sentinel release, and Wake.ts:80 calls `#press(true)` before the request. Wake.test.ts:144 checks `aria-pressed` after an external release, but that test composes no scope, so the plugin projection never runs there either.

findings.claim: The `probes visibility recovery` case asserts that no visibilitychange fired and that the request count stayed at 1. It therefore pins nothing about the handler at Wake.ts:31-38, including its retained-intent gate. The departure row records the real hidden-to-visible transition as unestablished. The gate itself, though, is reachable with a dispatched `visibilitychange` while `visibilityState` is `'visible'`, and no case exercises it. guides/veneer.md:1178-1179 still states recovery as behavior, and :1205 lists "visibility probes" among the controller proofs.
findings.scenario: Change Wake.ts:34 to `if (!this.#pressed && ...)`, or to `if (true)`. Each change makes the controller re-request a lock on visibility return after the user toggled off, or never re-request with retained intent. All wake tests stay green. The listener-count case in plugins.test.ts:205-223 checks only that the listener is registered and removed, not what it does.
findings.evidence: Wake.test.ts:169-170: `expect(visibility.calls).toEqual([]); expect(requests.count).toBe(1)`. Wake.ts:34: `if (this.#pressed && element.ownerDocument.visibilityState === 'visible') void this.acquire()`. Guide departure row at guides/veneer.md:1826: "Recovery after a real hidden-to-visible transition remains unestablished."

findings.claim: The guide and TSDoc say the error event carries the platform rejection unchanged. In an insecure context, or a browser without the Screen Wake Lock API, `navigator.wakeLock` is undefined. The `.request('screen')` property access then throws a TypeError from the controller's own code, and the error event relays that TypeError instead of a platform rejection.
findings.scenario: A developer opens the showcase over plain http on a LAN IP to test on a phone. `navigator.wakeLock` is undefined there because the context is not secure. Clicking Keep screen on emits `error.vn.wake` with `detail.error` set to `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'request')`. That is not a platform `DOMException`, so a consumer that branches on `error.name` (`NotAllowedError`) cannot recognize it. The controller also writes `aria-pressed="true"` before the throw.
findings.evidence: Wake.ts:82-84: `await (this.#element.ownerDocument.defaultView ?? window).navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')` is inside the try, and the catch at :101-105 emits it as `{ error }`. Wake.ts:64-65 TSDoc: "Reports the unchanged platform rejection through the error event". guides/veneer.md:1175: "Carries the platform rejection unchanged and clears intent."

findings.claim: The guide says an item can move between the hosts of its group, that the group order is the hosts' document order, and that Alt+Arrow crossing moves to the previous or next host in document order (line 1608). The code builds the group only from hosts that already have a registered controller (`#group()` at src/browser/drags/Drag.ts:118-131 uses `this.#context.component(host)`), so a group host with no controller is left out of the group.
findings.scenario: The scope boots with `<ul data-vn-drag="board" aria-label="Inbox">` and the page renders an empty `<ul data-vn-drag="board" aria-label="Done">` later. A keyboard user focuses an Inbox grip and presses Alt+ArrowRight, or clicks a `--forward` command button. `#group()` returns only Inbox, so `#cross` finds no next host and emits nothing. Done is the next host in document order, but neither keyboard nor command input can reach it. Only a native mouse dragenter over Done constructs its controller.
findings.evidence: Drag.ts:118-131: `const controller = host instanceof realm.HTMLElement && host.getAttribute('data-vn-drag') === group ? this.#context.component(host) : undefined; if (controller) controllers.push(controller)`. Drag.ts:470: crossing is gated on `this.#group().length`. The boot selector `[data-vn-drag]` in plugins.ts runs only at scope boot.

findings.claim: The `error.vn.wake` row says the event carries the platform rejection unchanged, and line 1177 says acquisition requires a secure context. In an insecure context `navigator.wakeLock` is undefined. `acquire()` then dereferences `.request` on undefined and reports the engine's own TypeError, which is not a platform rejection. The copier handles the same case by building a `NotAllowedError` DOMException.
findings.scenario: A page is served over plain http on a LAN address and the user clicks a `command="--wake"` button. `navigator.wakeLock` is undefined, so `undefined.request('screen')` throws a TypeError inside the try block. `error.vn.wake` then fires with `detail.error` set to a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") instead of a platform `DOMException`.
findings.evidence: src/browser/wakes/Wake.ts:82-84: `const sentinel = await (this.#element.ownerDocument.defaultView ?? window).navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')`, and the catch at Wake.ts:101-105 emits `{ error }` unchanged. Compare Copier.ts:59-60, which builds `new realm.DOMException('The clipboard needs a secure context', 'NotAllowedError')` when the API is absent.

findings.claim: The `result.vn.copier` row says a failure carries the platform's `DOMException`. This range adds a path where the copier builds the DOMException itself: when the clipboard API is absent, the copier throws its own `NotAllowedError` with the message "The clipboard needs a secure context", and the result event carries it.
findings.scenario: A page is served from an insecure origin, so `navigator.clipboard` is undefined. The user clicks Copy after transient activation has expired, or `execCommand('copy')` fails. `result.vn.copier` carries `error` as a DOMException the copier constructed, not one from the platform, which contradicts the row. The prose at line 1485 describes this synthesized error, so the table row and the paragraph after it disagree.
